person_made_it: Eric's real year as six plates from the brief: Dad (James, Henry, and Oscar), the Iverson-Johnson House 1898, Cider Camp, GGP Executive Producer, the day job (product owner), the Dragon Table; plates cut from the Dragon House emblem he designed (seal.png as the art reference); helpers are Crystal, Gordon and the boys in their stated colors.
emcee_who_is_speaking: Darby, openly, for Gordon: the start card says 'For Eric, from Gordon and Darby'; the marquee lines are short stage calls, no one is impersonated.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: night under lantern strings, a painted bandstand with warm spotlight pools on the boards.
did_the_click_pay_me: every tap spins a plate with a rising whoosh pitched to its speed, gold sparks, motion-blur ghosts and a glint; low plates wobble, sway and pulse; a falling plate is caught by a gold-leaf hand with a name tag and a chime; the finale lifts every plate on its own with a celesta sweep, confetti cannons, a crowd cheer and a folk-band fanfare.
works_for_the_recipient: Played to the end with real input in WebKit 390x844 (touch), Chromium 1920x1080 (mouse) and Chromium 2560x1440 (keys 1 to 6); 0 page errors, no sideways scroll; PC layout runs six poles across the stage with key hints, hover glow and full screen; JS off shows the full story, the six plates, the line, and the link back.
taught_me_something: rosemaling, the Norwegian folk painting, and the game's one rule: nobody loses, a dropped plate always gets caught.
told_me_the_truth: only brief facts appear; the boys get colors and nothing else; Cider Camp's subline says only 'the camp you run'; helpers go to whichever plate is lowest, so no one is assigned an invented role.
weakest: The hands are painted art that rises into place rather than animating fingers, and the score speeds up by playbackRate, which also lifts its pitch about three semitones by the end; a second, faster ElevenLabs take crossfaded in would be the honest fix.
